An open-loop control system operates without feedback, meaning it cannot adjust its output based on actual performance or disturbances.  
This leads to inaccuracy because any unaccounted changes in the system or environment will cause deviations from the desired output.  
It is also unreliable because it cannot self-correct errors or adapt to unexpected conditions.  
Both inaccuracy and unreliability are recognized disadvantages of open-loop systems.
